page: Hetzner Cloud ccx33 is a dedicated CPU virtual server running on the QEMU hypervisor. It features an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor with 8 dedicated vCPUs, mapped from 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The CPU operates at a base speed of 2.0 GHz and includes 32 KB L1d cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 31.0 GB of RAM, providing approximately 3.91 GB of memory per core, and includes 240 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. It does not include any complimentary public IPv4 addresses or GPU accelerators.

In benchmark testing, the ccx33 demonstrates strong single-core performance, as evidenced by its stress-ng single-core CPU score of 3061.27 and a strong bzip3 single-threaded decompression rate of 13.79 GB/sec. Multi-core performance is average, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 7266.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 14721.51. Memory performance is mixed; while cached small-block read bandwidth is average at 585.69 GB/sec, large-block uncached read bandwidth is weak at 38.5 GB/sec. Similarly, LLM inference prompt processing for a medium 7B model is weak at 22.49 tokens/sec, though text generation for the same model remains average at 9.31 tokens/sec.

The dedicated CPU allocation provides predictable compute performance without resource contention, making this server a cost-efficient option for workloads requiring sustained CPU utilization. Given its balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and local NVMe SSD storage, the ccx33 is suited for general-purpose workloads, software compilation, database operations, and static web serving.
